note: From the OpenStreetMap export (main API, 13 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs) and the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/ryder-brow.jpg), at real scale across the line like the tracks. Positive v is north-north-east; the line runs west-north-west towards Manchester. Two short side platforms (about 82 m), 1.68 m outside the Marple line's two tracks; the halt's is the real platform 2 on the south-west side, for trains towards Manchester. Levenshulme Road crosses over the line on a skewed bridge just south of the platforms (drawn square across the line). There is no footbridge: passengers cross on Levenshulme Road (the way across): from the south end of platform 2 a path climbs the bank to the road, drawn as steps along the line up to the bridge, and from the middle of platform 1 a ramp runs up behind it to the road at the bridge's north-east end. The platforms take a two-car train; trains stop 12 m north of the station's point so a two-car one stands on them as they are and a four-car one once they're extended north (the bridge is in the way to the south), and a six-car one stands off the north end, as at a real short platform, which `longest` says. The bus stop is Levenshulme Road / outside Ryder Brow Station, on the road's approach to the bridge. No photographs: the shelters, lamps and boards are the usual Northern ones from memory, the station (opened in 1985) is unstaffed with no booking office (from memory), and the lifts and canopy are the game's. Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).
